content.summary: The complete-C5 bridge and the degree-17 P10 empty-internal contradiction survive the inspected structural and literal counterexample checks. I independently reproduced the degree-20 internal coefficient margin and the degree-17 scalar maximum. An explicit degree-16 example confirms why internal cost must be retained; the current proof does retain it. No necessary revision arose in this scope. Imported classifications and uninspected nonempty-orbit model rows retain their stated assurance limits.

findings.statement: The unconditional assertion that a complete C5 pair-link forces global degree at most 15 is false when internal members are present. A six-member C5 component plus a disjoint P10 gives a literal counterexample at degree 16 with one internal member.
findings.disposition: This is a counterexample to an overstrong interpretation, not to the manuscript. internal-proof.md uses d(y)-I_y<=15 before internal exclusion, and the degree-17 empty case applies d(y)<=15 only after I_y=0.

checks.scope: Complete-C5 lemma at size 16, including exceptional structures
checks.method: Read C5-internal-compatibility.md, General structural lemma, Proof at size sixteen, and Sizes seventeen through twenty; reconstructed each structural alternative.
checks.observation: The R16 alternative has only degrees four and six, excluding the required degree-five point. A B4 partition with a P-type component has disjoint supports using the actual anchor to exclude deleted blocks. If both parts are Q8, a core point has a triangle or C4 in its link, incompatible with a complete C5; a shared leaf has degree at most two. Thus the C5 component is confined to its six points, and its non-star members are internal cycle covers even when the opposite part is an arbitrary I6 or I7.

checks.scope: Necessity and correct use of internal-completion cost
checks.method: Constructed and directly tested the literal SF3 family {012,015,023,034,045,124} union a disjoint copy of P10 on 6,...,11; then coned it with a fresh point 20 and checked every three-member sunflower.
checks.observation: Both the 16-triple family and its SF4 cone are sunflower-free. Point 20 has degree 16; the pair-link of 0 and 20 is a complete C5; exactly one member through 20 is internal on {20,1,2,3,4,5}. Hence d(20)-I_20=15 while d(20)<=15 is false. This matches C5-internal-compatibility.md, Translation to a central C5 neighbor, and the retained cost in internal-proof.md, Weighted incidence certificate.

checks.scope: Local51 geometric interface for the degree-20 internal certificate
checks.method: Read internal-proof.md and local51-geometry-check.md; checked the literal anchor dictionary against P10 and D8/D9 in pinned MU42/TRACE_FOUNDATIONS.md, lines 80-109.
checks.observation: At anchor {x,1,3,5}, the occupied complementary triple classes have distinct exterior points 2,0,4. When singleton indices 1 and 3 are large, D9 therefore excludes e=1 and a=2, while D8 gives a<=2 beforehand. The small-singleton implication uses the universal degree-18 high-link decomposition, not a mu42 bootstrap. The local degree identities and the stated W<=51 case split are consistent with these actual-anchor hypotheses.

checks.scope: Degree-20 internal weighted cover on arbitrary exterior completions
checks.method: Reconstructed the row list in an independent bounded Python calculation; represented each of all 794 core traces by an actual four-set with fresh exterior points; tested literal sunflower intersections with M=0123 and every root cone.
checks.observation: Exactly 372 traces have a blocking cone. The 422 survivors have coefficient histogram {5:357,6:14,8:1,10:35,15:14,17:1}; the marker coefficient is 8 and the weighted right-hand side is 241. Thus 5r+3<=241 gives r<=47. Proper-trace multiplicities remain valid because the inequality sums over actual members. This reproduces the finite cover in internal-proof.md without importing or executing its writing checker.

checks.scope: Degree-17 P10 pair pools and arbitrary opposite support
checks.method: Read D17-P10-ordinary-closure.md, Residual trace counts, Universal C5 pair-pool bound, and Ten-cone average; independently checked all 60 C5 partner-pair avoidance witnesses and literal P10 incidence counts.
checks.observation: Singleton, pair and triple traces meet respectively 5,8,and 9 or 10 P10 blocks. The two disjoint exterior-edge cases give actual sunflower witnesses, so the exterior edge graph is intersecting and multiplicity-aware pair/triple capacities give b_y<=6. The combined trace-0/trace-1 pool is intersecting because a P10 block avoids every two-point trace. None of these arguments restricts or classifies the seven opposite triples or other exterior points.

checks.method: Reconstructed the incidence calculation and exhaustively checked the bounded integer scalar domain H,P,E>=0, H+P+E<=51, H+2P+3E<=60, P<=18 and P+E>=24.
checks.observation: The maximum of 5H+8P+10E is 234, attained at (H,P,E)=(6,18,6), whereas ten actual root cones require at least 10*(41-17)=240. The degree-sum bound subtracts exactly 30 prescribed Y-incidences from six degree caps of 15. The caps follow from the complete-C5 lemma and empty internal family, not from an assumed finite support for the opposite I7.
